ee6ad71b-9c92-4578-a0ef-9e90fab6cc97.title: Software Engineer New Grad - Software
ee6ad71b-9c92-4578-a0ef-9e90fab6cc97.description: <div class= content-intro ><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>NEW GRADUATE ENGINEER, SOFTWARE - 26/ 27 (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>At SpaceX we’re leveraging our experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s most advanced broadband internet system. Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation and is providing fast, reliable internet to millions of users worldwide. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system – thousands of satellites, consumer receivers that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing, and the software that brings it all together. We’ve only begun to scratch the surface of Starlink’s potential global impact and are looking for best-in-class engineers to help maximize Starlink’s utility for communities and businesses around the globe.</p> <p>As arguably SpaceX s most complex software engineering challenge, Starlink offers a variety of areas within software engineering that you can focus. As a Software Engineer on the Starlink program, you will be solving challenges underpinning every aspect of the program’s growth. The teams and areas you could have an impact on could include, but are not limited to:</p> <ul> <li>Next generation networking technologies to direct data through an ever-changing network of satellites, ground stations, planes and users.</li> <li>Firmware, embedded and controls software running on custom hardware that flies the world’s largest fleet of spacecraft.</li> <li>Infrastructure and tools to enable rapid development and reliable deployment of our code to dynamic production environments.</li> <li>Measurement system software and hardware, supporting our in-house RF Silicon designs.</li> <li>Full life cycle development of Starlink.com and our Mobile/Enterprise platforms.</li> <li>Physic based software engineering to design and simulate the orbital life cycle of the Starlink constellation. nbsp;</li> </ul> <p>Our software engineers are responsible for the complete lifecycle of the software they create, including development, testing, and support. We expect our engineers to close the feedback loop between software design and real-world performance. In this role, your software will have a meaningful and measurable impact on the world.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Develop highly reliable, real-time software.</li> <li>Participate in and lead architecture, design, and code reviews.</li> <li>Develop prototypes and manage experiments to prove out key design concepts.</li> <li>Collaborate with other engineers, from other engineering disciplines, to plan and organize the development of our products.</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in computer science, engineering, math, or other STEM discipline.</li> <li>Professional development experience in C, C++, Python, C# or another object oriented language (internship experience is applicable).</li> <li>Graduating in the class of 2026 or 2027.</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Strong professional/project experience writing software in a production environment.</li> <li>Developed, debugged and deployed software that has been used in real world applications/projects.</li> <li>Creative approach to problem solving, exceptional analytical skills and engineering fundamentals.</li> <li>Excellent communication skills both written and verbal.</li> <li>Ability to work effectively in a dynamic environment with changing needs and requirements.</li> <li>Experience with networking protocols (UDP, TCP/IP, etc) and distributed systems.</li> <li>Experience in security issues associated with distributed systems and internet services.</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Must be willing to work extended hours and weekends as needed.</li> </ul> <p><strong>COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:</strong><br><br>Pay Range:<br>Level 1: $125,000.00 - $165,000.00<br>Level 2: $145,000.00 - $200,000.00<br><br></p> <p>Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.</p> <p>Base salary is just one part of your total rewards package at SpaceX. You may also be eligible for long-term incentives, in the form of company stock or long-term cash awards, as well as potential discretionary bonuses and the ability to purchase additional stock at a discount through an Employee Stock Purchase Plan. You will also receive access to comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, short and long-term disability insurance, life insurance, paid parental leave, and various other discounts and perks. You may also accrue 3 weeks of paid vacation and will be eligible for 10 or more paid holidays per year. Employees in Washington State accrue paid sick time in compliance with state and federal law. Company shuttles are offered to employees for roundtrip travel from select Seattle locations to the SpaceX Redmond office Monday to Friday.</p><div class= content-conc
ee6ad71b-9c92-4578-a0ef-9e90fab6cc97.fit_reason: Starlink explicitly wants networking (TCP/IP, UDP), distributed systems, security, and infra/deployment tooling — a direct hit on the candidate's Raft/LSM/MVCC KV store, backend microservices, and cloud/K8s/Terraform background, with C/C++/Python matching the required languages and the class-of-2027 graduation date accepted; minor deductions for the Redmond-only location, the embedded/RF/physics-sim teams being off-profile, the ITAR "US person" (citizen/green card) bar being stricter than plain US work authorization, and the explicit extended-hours/weekends expectation.
ee6ad71b-9c92-4578-a0ef-9e90fab6cc97.tc_basis: SpaceX posts base directly: Level 1 $125–165k, Level 2 $145–200k; new grads land L1, typically ~$130–150k base. Add long-term incentives (company stock/long-term cash, illiquid private shares) plus possible discretionary bonus and ESPP discount, worth roughly $10–35k/yr in nominal value. Band reflects L1 with a small chance of L2 for a strong candidate. Estimate, not fact.

59376e30-4b2e-4ba7-8acb-1cf947065c18.description: <div class= content-intro ><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>NEW GRADUATE ENGINEER, SOFTWARE SECURITY - 26/ 27 (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>At SpaceX we’re leveraging our experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s most advanced broadband internet system. Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation and serves millions of users worldwide. We design, build, and operate all parts of the system – thousands of satellites and all of the space-ground infrastructure necessary for a constellation of that size.<br><br>As we scale the constellation to hundreds of thousands of satellites, and become a foundation of global connectivity both on earth (and in space), we are looking for excellent engineers to help us build secure, defensible systems from the ground up.<br><br>As a Security Software Engineer you will influence the security of software across our space and terrestrial systems. Ideally, you have notable skills in one or more of the following:</p> <ul> <li>Software engineering</li> <li>Applied cryptography</li> <li>Network security</li> <li>Operating system security</li> <li>Secure/Authenticated boot</li> <li>Incident response and adversary detection</li> <li>Vulnerability research</li> </ul> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Design and build security critical infrastructure for Starlink</li> <li>Develop security features for Starlink systems, including our router, dish, gateways, and satellites</li> <li>Design security into factory processes and provide network services in support of this</li> <li>Maintain existing production systems and improve security posture via both direct implementation and recommendations to other teams</li> <li>Build prototypes and help identify, design, and test security improvements</li> <li>Further our mission of providing secure and reliable Internet to underserved communities nbsp;</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor s degree in computer science or another STEM discipline</li> <li>Experience with one or more software development languages (i.e. Python, C++, Golang)</li> <li>Experience designing and implementing security solutions for operating systems, distributed systems, or other enterprise/large-scale infrastructure</li> <li>Graduating in the class of 2026 or 2027</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Designing secure systems nbsp;</li> <li>Experience contributing security improvements to complex systems</li> <li>Experience working with special purpose security hardware such as Trusted Platform Modules (TPMs) and Hardware Security Modules (HSMs)</li> <li>Experienced in navigating large, complex, interactive systems</li> <li>Flexibility, communicating clearly, and establishing and maintaining productive working relationships with other engineering teams</li> <li>Ability to work both independently and in a team</li> <li>Demonstrated ability to deal with ambiguity and to learn new technologies quickly</li> <li>Advanced degree in a technical or engineering discipline nbsp;</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Must be willing to work extended hours and weekends as needed</li> </ul> <strong>COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:</strong><br><br> Pay Range:<br> Level 1: $130,000.00 - $165,000.00<br>Level 2: $150,000.00 - $200,000.00<br><br> <p>Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.</p> <p>Base salary is just one part of your total rewards package at SpaceX. You may also be eligible for long-term incentives, in the form of company stock or long-term cash awards, as well as potential discretionary bonuses and the ability to purchase additional stock at a discount through an Employee Stock Purchase Plan. You will also receive access to comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, short and long-term disability insurance, life insurance, paid parental leave, and various other discounts and perks. You may also accrue 3 weeks of paid vacation and will be eligible for 10 or more paid holidays per year. Employees in Washington State accrue paid sick time in compliance with state and federal law. Company shuttles are offered to employees for roundtrip travel from select Seattle locations to the SpaceX Redmond office Monday to Friday.</p><div class= content-conclusion ><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR <a href= https://www.pmddtc.state.gov/?id=ddtc_kb_article_page amp;sys_id=24d528fddbfc930044f9ff621f961987 >here</a>. nbsp;</li&

0e79e8bc-db11-456f-97e4-54fea42c6715.description: <div class= content-intro ><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. 0e79e8bc-db11-456f-97e4-54fea42c6715.tc_basis: Posting lists Level 1 base of $135k-$175k (new grads almost always L1, realistically $140-155k base in Palo Alto). Add SpaceX long-term incentives (private company stock or long-term cash awards), discretionary bonus, and ESPP discount. Estimate, not fact.

690c397c-b387-4787-a4e9-78adb2342b32.title: Systems Analyst - Leap Program
690c397c-b387-4787-a4e9-78adb2342b32.description: July 2027 - Leap Systems Analyst Skip to main content Sign In Fidelity Careers July 2027 - Leap Systems Analyst page is loaded July 2027 - Leap Systems Analyst Apply locations Westlake, TX Durham, NC Merrimack, NH time type Full time posted on Posted Yesterday job requisition id 2133879 Job Description: Fidelity Leap Program Note: Fidelity will not provide immigration sponsorship for this position Launch your tech career by building real solutions that impact millions. Ready to go beyond the classroom? Build technology that powers financial outcomes for millions of customers — supporting individuals, employers, and institutions across a global, diversified business with trillions in assets. Join Fidelity’s Leap Program and start your career alongside thousands of technologists shaping the future of financial services. About the Leap Program Our 10-week immersive program is designed to help you transition from college to a full-time technology career. You’ll gain hands-on experience, build production-ready skills, and grow alongside a cohort of peers, all while solving real, complex business challenges. What you’ll gain: Real-world technology experience from day one Mentorship from experienced engineers and leaders A strong peer network that lasts beyond the program A clear path to continued growth at Fidelity Program Highlights Learn by Building Work on real projects in a supportive environment where you can experiment, learn, and make an impact. AI-Native Development Use AI tools as part of your daily workflow, learning how to apply them responsibly to modern engineering challenges. Cohort Experience Join a group of peers in an in-person, team-based setting with built-in support, coaching, and collaboration. Career Acceleration This isn’t just a program, it’s the start of your career. Continue growing with meaningful work, mentorship, and long-term opportunities at Fidelity. The Role We’re looking for curious, driven systems analysts who want to understand how technology and business come together to solve problems and deliver value for customers. In this role, you will: Support analysis activities by participating in stakeholder discussions, capturing requirements, and helping clarify ambiguities with guidance from senior analysts and team members Work on real projects from start to finish, gaining exposure to the full delivery lifecycle including requirements, architecture, design, testing, and implementation Create and maintain documentation such as user stories, functional specifications, acceptance criteria, and process/data flow diagrams using standard tools and templates, while describing basic concepts and major activities associated with requirements analysis Develop an understanding of business context, system workflows, data flows, and upstream/downstream dependencies across the technology landscape Support basic data analysis activities, including running queries, validating test data, and investigating simple data or system issues. while identifying gaps between current systems and future business needs. Assist with testing efforts by creating test cases, executing tests, analyzing results, and logging defects Explore emerging tools and technologies, including AI, and learn how to apply them responsibly to improve analysis and delivery outcomes Contribute as part of a team focused on delivering solutions that help customers achieve their long-term financial goals Skills You Bring To be eligible, applicants must have earned or be on track to earn a bachelor’s degree in computer science, Software Engineering, or a related field by the start date. Familiarity with requirements gathering, documentation, or systems analysis concepts (academic or internship experience) Foundational awareness of data concepts (e.g., data flows, data validation, or querying) Strong analytical thinking and problem-solving skills Ability to break down problems and ask thoughtful, clarifying questions Familiarity with diagramming tools such as Visio or Drawio Hands-on project or internship experience (preferred) Strong written and verbal communication skills Ability to collaborate and thrive in a fast-paced, team environment Curiosity, attention to detail, and a passion for continuous learning Why Fidelity? Work on systems and products used by millions Access to diverse tech stack and AI tools Structured career development and mobility Strong mentorship culture Competitive benefits and stability If you’re excited to learn how technology enables business outcomes and want to build a strong foundation in systems analysis, Fidelity is a great fit for you. We hire for fundamentals, learning agility and problem-solving, and are committed to help you grow. Apply today! Fidelity’s Onsite Working Model Fidelity is transitioning to a full-time onsite working model through a phased rollout across regions and roles. Currently, some roles and locations require 100% onsite presence, while others require less. Onsite expectations are likely to evolve as the rollout continues. This transition does not apply to fully remote roles. Certifications: Category: Information Technology Please be advised that Fidelity’s business is governed by the provisions of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, the Investment Advisers Act of 1940, the Investment Company Act of 1940, ERISA, numerous state laws governing securities, investment and retirement-related financial activities and the rules and regulations of numerous self-regulatory organizations, including FINRA, among others. Those laws and regulations may restrict Fidelity from hiring and/or associating with individuals with certain Criminal Histories. 1f50cd90-b872-416f-8df0-0c482c23b642.description: <div class= content-intro ><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>NEW GRADUATE ENGINEER, SOFTWARE SECURITY - 26/ 27 (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>At SpaceX we’re leveraging our experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s most advanced broadband internet system. Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation and serves millions of users worldwide. We design, build, and operate all parts of the system – thousands of satellites and all of the space-ground infrastructure necessary for a constellation of that size.<br><br>As we scale the constellation to hundreds of thousands of satellites, and become a foundation of global connectivity both on earth (and in space), we are looking for excellent engineers to help us build secure, defensible systems from the ground up.<br><br>As a Security Software Engineer you will influence the security of software across our space and terrestrial systems. Ideally, you have notable skills in one or more of the following:</p> <ul> <li>Software engineering</li> <li>Applied cryptography</li> <li>Network security</li> <li>Operating system security</li> <li>Secure/Authenticated boot</li> <li>Incident response and adversary detection</li> <li>Vulnerability research</li> </ul> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Design and build security critical infrastructure for Starlink</li> <li>Develop security features for Starlink systems, including our router, dish, gateways, and satellites</li> <li>Design security into factory processes and provide network services in support of this</li> <li>Maintain existing production systems and improve security posture via both direct implementation and recommendations to other teams</li> <li>Build prototypes and help identify, design, and test security improvements</li> <li>Further our mission of providing secure and reliable Internet to underserved communities nbsp;</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor s degree in computer science or another STEM discipline</li> <li>Experience with one or more software development languages (i.e. Python, C++, Golang)</li> <li>Experience designing and implementing security solutions for operating systems, distributed systems, or other enterprise/large-scale infrastructure</li> <li>Graduating in the class of 2026 or 2027</li> </ul> <p><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Designing secure systems nbsp;</li> <li>Experience contributing security improvements to complex systems</li> <li>Experience working with special purpose security hardware such as Trusted Platform Modules (TPMs) and Hardware Security Modules (HSMs)</li> <li>Experienced in navigating large, complex, interactive systems</li> <li>Flexibility, communicating clearly, and establishing and maintaining productive working relationships with other engineering teams</li> <li>Ability to work both independently and in a team</li> <li>Demonstrated ability to deal with ambiguity and to learn new technologies quickly</li> <li>Advanced degree in a technical or engineering discipline nbsp;</li> </ul> <p><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Must be willing to work extended hours and weekends as needed</li> </ul><div class= content-conclusion ><p><strong>ITAR REQUIREMENTS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR <a href= https://www.pmddtc.state.gov/?id=ddtc_kb_article_page amp;sys_id=24d528fddbfc930044f9ff621f961987 >here</a>. nbsp;</li> </ul> <p>SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with SpaceX is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.</p> <p>Applicants wishing to view a copy of SpaceX’s Affirmative Action Plan for veterans and individuals with disabilities, or applicants requiring reasonable accommodation to the application/interview process should reach out to nbsp;<a href= mailto:EEOCompliance@spacex.com >EEOCompliance@spacex.com</a><em>. nbsp;</em></p></div>
1f50cd90-b872-416f-8df0-0c482c23b642.fit_reason: Systems/security concentration plus distributed-systems and C/C++/Python/Rust experience map directly onto securing OS/distributed/large-scale infrastructure, and the class-of-2027 eligibility and ITAR-only (no clearance) requirement fit; docked for Bastrop TX location, no remote, mandatory extended hours/weekends, and no AI-infra overlap.
1f50cd90-b872-416f-8df0-0c482c23b642.tc_basis: SpaceX new-grad SWE base generally ~$120-145k with stock options adding ~$15-35k/yr; Starlink security is a core-mission team so it trends mid-to-upper in that range. Estimate only — SpaceX skews cash-lighter and equity-heavier than big tech.

1436f890-5733-4b9e-ad61-4df307e22f43.title: Software Engineer New Grad - Software - Starlink
1436f890-5733-4b9e-ad61-4df307e22f43.description: <div class= content-intro ><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of nbsp;enabling human life on Mars.</p></div><p><strong>NEW GRADUATE ENGINEER, SOFTWARE - 26/ 27 (STARLINK)</strong></p> <p>At SpaceX we’re leveraging our experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s most advanced broadband internet system. Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation and is providing fast, reliable internet to millions of users worldwide. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system – thousands of satellites, consumer receivers that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing, and the software that brings it all together. We’ve only begun to scratch the surface of Starlink’s potential global impact and are looking for best-in-class engineers to help maximize Starlink’s utility for communities and businesses around the globe.</p> <p>As arguably SpaceX s most complex software engineering challenge, Starlink offers a variety of areas within software engineering that you can focus. As a Software Engineer on the Starlink program, you will be solving challenges underpinning every aspect of the program’s growth. The teams and areas you could have an impact on could include, but are not limited to:</p> <ul> <li>Next generation networking technologies to direct data through an ever-changing network of satellites, ground stations, planes and users.</li> <li>Firmware, embedded and controls software running on custom hardware that flies the world’s largest fleet of spacecraft.</li> <li>Infrastructure and tools to enable rapid development and reliable deployment of our code to dynamic production environments.</li> <li>Measurement system software and hardware, supporting our in-house RF Silicon designs.</li> <li>Physic based software engineering to design and simulate the orbital life cycle of the Starlink constellation. nbsp;</li> <li>Develop software running on custom hardware that is deployed to millions of devices around the world</li> <li>Create infrastructure and tools for rapid and reliable deployment of our code to our customers no matter where they are</li> <li>Write software for Starlink’s custom phased array and modem silicon</li> </ul> <p>Our software engineers are responsible for the complete lifecycle of the software they create, including development, testing, and support. We expect our engineers to close the feedback loop between software design and real-world performance. In this role, your software will have a meaningful and measurable impact on the world.</p> <p><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Develop highly reliable, real-time software.</li> <li>Participate in and lead architecture, design, and code reviews.</li> <li>Develop prototypes and manage experiments to prove out key design concepts.</li> <li>Collaborate with other engineers, from other engineering disciplines, to plan and organize the development of our products.</li> </ul> <p><strong>BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s degree in computer science, USD $119,100.00/Yr. mail_outline Get future jobs matching this search Login or Register Job Description Overview At PNNL, our core capabilities are divided among major departments that we refer to as Directorates within the Lab, focused on a specific area of scientific research or other function, with its own leadership team and dedicated budget. Our Science Technology directorates include National Security, Integrated Discovery Sciences, and Energy and Environment. In addition, we have an Environmental Molecular Sciences Laboratory, a Department of Energy, Office of Science user facility housed on the PNNL campus. The Energy and Environment Directorate delivers science and technology solutions for the nation’s biggest energy and environmental challenges. Our more than 1,700 staff support the Department of Energy (DOE), delivering on key DOE mission areas including: modernizing our nation’s power grid to maintain a reliable, affordable, secure, and resilient electricity delivery infrastructure; research, development, validation, and effective utilization of renewable energy and efficiency technologies that improve the affordability, reliability, resiliency, and security of the American energy system; and resolving complex issues in nuclear science, energy, and environmental management. The Earth Systems Science Division, part of the Energy and Environment Directorate, provides leadership and solutions that advance Earth system opportunities for energy systems and national security. We are a multidisciplinary division connected by a shared commitment to innovate and collaborate towards solving complex problems in the dynamic Earth system. Responsibilities Post Doctorate Responsibilities include: Lead end-to-end data flow for field-collected sensor data: ingest, quality control, duplicate detection, time synchronization, event grouping, tracking, uncertainty characterization, archiving, and visualization Maintain and improve batch decoders and downstream processing code in MATLAB and Python, refactoring for reliability, performance, reproducibility, and maintainability Design scalable workflows for high-volume processing using parallelization, HPC schedulers, workflow managers, and containerized environments Develop and evaluate physics-informed ML, hybrid mechanistic-ML, Bayesian, and state-space models that incorporate physical constraints, sensor geometry, timing uncertainty, hydrodynamic context, and biological domain knowledge Implement automated testing, continuous integration, code review standards, documentation, and operational monitoring/logging for research pipelines Perform statistical analyses and visualization; synthesize engineering and biological insights into manuscripts, technical reports, and presentations Collaborate with field teams to align processing with deployment metadata, surveys, coordinate systems, and reference frames for tracking outputs Mentor students and junior staff and coordinate across multidisciplinary teams. Primarily office and computational work; occasional field support may involve work on or near water, small vessels, and variable weather conditions. Required safety training and personal protective equipment will be provided. Qualifications Minimum Qualifications: Candidates must have received a PhD within the past five years (60 months) or within the next 8 months from an accredited college or university. Preferred Qualifications: PhD in Mechanical, Electrical, or Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Statistics or Data Science, Applied Mathematics, Fisheries, Oceanography, Ecology, or a related field. Demonstrated research record, including first-author peer-reviewed publications. Advanced proficiency in at least one scientific programming language (Python, MATLAB, or R) and the ability to translate algorithms across languages. Strong background in signal processing, time-series analysis, statistical modeling, machine learning, or data assimilation for noisy sensor data. Experience building reproducible research workflows using version control, testing, packaging, documentation, and code review. Experience working with large datasets using relational databases, efficient file formats, or data engineering best practices. Proficiency in Linux and HPC or cloud environments, including scripting and automation of data processing workflows. Excellent scientific writing and communication skills, including methods documentation and clear visualization. Ability to work independently, set priorities, and deliver in a collaborative research environment. Experience with acoustic telemetry, passive or active sensing, underwater acoustics, or other sensor-network data. Experience with physics-informed, mechanistic, or otherwise model-constrained approaches to machine learning and statistical inference. Experience mentoring students or junior technical staff. Hazardous Working Conditions/Environment Not Applicable Testing Designated Position This is not a Testing Designated Position (TDP). About PNNL Pacific Northwest National

The work will require some knowledge of algorithms, data structures, software development and hardware platforms, as well as attention to detail, and will emphasize problem solving and rapid development for the scientific community we serve. The position will interact with our Community Software Facility, as well as a variety of software engineers and scientific leadership on targeted, strategic priorities. This Software Engineer position is part of the computer engineering group within NSF NCAR's CGD Laboratory. CGD is home to approximately 130 staff members, along with visiting researchers from around the world. Together, they advance the understanding of Earth system variability and change while addressing the risks of environmental change through collaborative, innovative, and inclusive research. More information about CGD can be found online at https://www.cgd.ucar.edu/. Job Description Application Deadline: This position will be posted until 11:59 pm MDT on Monday, September 7, 2026. Visa Sponsorship and Relocation Assistance may be available to final candidate if eligible. Software Engineering Optimization: Participates in the enhancement of the CESM modeling ecosystem, targeting performance improvements, memory reductions, hardware portability (GPUs) and other key project needs. Collaborates with team members project stakeholders on proposed changes processes for integration into the model. Code Capability Analysis: Review and analyze existing modeling software capabilities to assess its structure, quality, and maintainability. Document findings, proposed changes, and technical decisions to support knowledge sharing across a wide team of scientists and engineers. Exploratory Development: Explore evaluate benchmarks in newer languages and paradigms Stay current with emerging tools, languages techniques relevant to software modernization. Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities Required: Proven ability to identify performance bottlenecks, inefficiencies, and other technical limitations through profiling, testing, and code analysis. Ability to recommend and implement modernization strategies, including refactoring legacy code, updating outdated libraries or frameworks, and applying current development standards and best practices. d7cea207-2957-4628-96f0-d1470db7594c.title: Software Engineer - Early Career
d7cea207-2957-4628-96f0-d1470db7594c.description: About Flow Flow Engineering is an AI-native requirements platform for modern engineering organizations, enabling hardware teams to collaborate with AI agents to design, validate, and evolve complex systems with speed and rigor. About the role *Note that this is NOT a new grad role! This role is for candidates with 0-2 YOE and can start full time right away. Flow is hiring early career software engineers to help build AI-powered capabilities that let teams author, review, and manage requirements more effectively. You will work alongside experienced engineers on agentic systems engineer and agentic domain engineer workflows, bringing AI into the center of how teams reason about their systems. This is a role for people early in their careers who are ready for an unusual amount of responsibility and autonomy. You will ship code to production in your first weeks, work directly with customers building rockets, satellites, and aircraft, and learn full-stack and AI engineering from people who have done it before. What you'll do Ship AI-powered features such as assisted requirement drafting, consistency checks, impact analysis, and intelligent suggestions for systems and domain engineers. Contribute to agentic workflows that help engineers explore designs, simulate changes, and validate requirements. Work across the stack, from backend services and APIs to the UI, so you own complete features rather than isolated pieces. Help build the surrounding infrastructure: data pipelines, evaluation harnesses, prompt and model management, and observability. Talk to customers, watch how they actually use what you built, and iterate quickly. Learn the domain. Requirements engineering for hardware is deep, unfamiliar to most software engineers, and the reason our product is hard to copy. About you You have less than two years of engineering experience. You have solid fundamentals in data structures, algorithms, and distributed systems, with a customer-minded, pragmatic approach to solving problems. Strong programming fundamentals and demonstrated ability to build real software, whether through internships, research, open source, or personal projects you can walk us through. Some exposure to modern LLM tooling, whether that is coursework, a side project, or an internship. You do not need production AI experience, but you should be genuinely interested in building with these systems. Clear communication. You can explain a technical decision and say when you are stuck. Comfortable with ambiguity and eager to work in a fast-moving environment where the roadmap changes and experiments are the norm. Our stack (AI-leaning) TypeScript/Node.js and Python for AI and backend services. Modern LLM APIs and orchestration libraries for building agentic workflows. Postgres and other managed cloud services for data and state.
d7cea207-2957-4628-96f0-d1470db7594c.fit_reason: The posting explicitly states this is NOT a new-grad role and requires someone who can start full time right away, which hard-blocks a May 2027 grad despite otherwise decent alignment (agentic/LLM systems, Python backend, distributed-systems fundamentals) — though the full-stack/UI ownership and TS/Node-leaning stack also pull away from his backend/infra core.

Cash-only realistic midpoint is closer to $140-150k.

As part of the Data Analytics (D A) team, the Software Evaluation Enablement Analyst will have the opportunity to partner with internal teams to build experience and knowledge across multiple systems and technical skills as they work with our Software Evaluation Enablement Manager to shape the software evaluation program. Learning and staying on top of technologies is crucial, and thankfully, VHB has a lot of smart folks to learn from! The initial focus will be building resources and structure around the program to empower VHBers with the ability to thoroughly and safely select technology solutions. Additionally, we envision this role taking part in the enablement of technology solutions and making sure they provide the most value to our teams. Come play a big role in shaping an evolving program that will have an impact on how we adopt technology. As the organization continues to mature its software evaluation process, under moderate supervision, this role will participate in the evaluation, selection, procurement, and implementation of new software solutions by serving as an IT partner to business teams, coordinating software evaluation efforts, providing structure consistency to the process, and contributing to making our software evaluation framework more scalable and self-service for business users. This includes developing and maintaining documentation, supporting intake and workflow coordination, and serving as a point of contact for questions related to the software evaluation process to ensure alignment with firm standards and business needs. Additionally, this role will support translating business needs into technical requirements and solutions and support the technical health of existing applications. They exercise independent judgment in handling routine project work and technical issues and escalate more complex matters as appropriate. This position offers remote work options from anywhere on the East Coast of the US, with work hours aligned to the EST time zone. Occasional travel, usually to our headquarters in Watertown, MA, is required. Please note: applicants must be legally authorized to work for VHB in the U.S. without employer sponsorship, now or in the future. Primary Duties Responsibilities Participates as a member of software evaluation and selection teams to assess potential technology solutions and ensure existing systems continue to meet business needs. Provides sustaining IT support to maintain the technical health, performance, and reliability of enterprise software systems and associated integrations. Initial focus on building partnerships with business teams to support upcoming software implementations with intent to develop product expertise and product management capabilities Works closely with business stakeholders to gather, analyze, and translate business needs into functional and technical system requirements and specifications. Serves as an IT liaison between business teams, software vendors, and internal IT delivery and infrastructure teams. Coordinates smaller software evaluation requests by partnering with business stakeholders and end users to collect requirements, clarify needs, assess use cases, and support the evaluation process from intake through selection. Maintains and supports software evaluation workflows and project tracking, including keeping evaluation stories, tasks, and statuses current and communicating progress to stakeholders. Facilitates and coordinates cross-functional review activities associated with software evaluations, including legal, IT security, architecture, procurement, or other required review points, and provides timely follow-up and status updates to stakeholders. Researches software vendors and prepares summary information on software categories, vendor capabilities, and solution options to support decision-making. Creates and maintains documentation related to software evaluations and application processes, including standard operating procedures, guides, how-to materials, workflow documentation, and best practices for internal users. Provides support for questions related to the software evaluation process and helps guide internal users toward established standards, procedures, and self-service resources. Analyzes system behavior, identifies technical gaps or risks, and recommends system enhancements or corrective actions. Supports system upgrades, patches, configuration changes, and ongoing optimization efforts. Develops and maintains technical documentation, including system specifications, workflows, integration touchpoints, and operational procedures. 6dda02da-3ec3-49ed-a963-fa6db627f830.title: Forward Deployed Engineer New Grad
6dda02da-3ec3-49ed-a963-fa6db627f830.description: LiteLLM is the world's most popular AI Gateway, trusted by top companies like Adobe, Netflix, and NASA. Our platform empowers developers by providing secure, reliable access to LLMs and adjacent services, and we're looking for a Forward Deployed Engineer (New Grad) to help our customers succeed with the leading OSS AI gateway. Because LiteLLM is a developer tool, this person needs to be technical. You'll dig into our customers' issues, understand them deeply, and unblock them. The core of this role is simple: work the queue, address tickets, and make our customers successful with the product. We're looking for someone who is obsessed with getting to the root cause of problems rather than applying surface-level fixes. The best people in this role understand the real depth of a problem before they solve it. Responsibilities - Own the support queue and work through tickets to drive customers to success - Diagnose customer issues and solve for the root cause, not just the symptom - Reproduce customer issues in their specific environments - Submit pull requests for bug fixes and improvements where needed - Act as the technical voice of the customer back to engineering What We're Looking For - A computer science degree from a top university (mandatory) - Strong technical fundamentals and eagerness to learn the LiteLLM product surface quickly - Obsessed with customers and making them successful with the product - Obsessed with solving root causes rather than patching over problems - Metrics-driven and hardworking, ready to move through a high volume of tickets - A strong bias toward understanding problems deeply Why Join LiteLLM? - Fast-paced growth environment with deep technical ownership. - Competitive salary, health, dental, and vision benefits, 401k plan with 3.5% match.

Streamline development setup and the onboarding experience. Work with platform teams to improve deployment processes, infrastructure integrations, and external tooling. Keep things fresh and modern in our codebase by adopting and leading migrations to better and faster tools. Partner with the AI team on our internal AI platform (which generates >60% of all merged PRs at Replit) to improve the Agent's output and shape strategy around its default stack. Help manage dependencies both internal (public and private) and external, including being the face of the company when interfacing with open-source libraries (e.g., sponsorships, upstream contributions). Required skills and experience: Strong proficiency in TypeScript and/or Go and/or Nix . Expertise in modern build systems and toolchains (e.g., Vite, webpack, esbuild, Go's build/module system). Proficiency with linters, formatters, testing frameworks, and code generation tools. Experience managing monorepos or large-scale codebases. Experience with AI-native development workflows — e.g., OpenCode, Claude Code, Cursor, custom agent skills. Open-source leadership or community contributions. Software Engineer - Entry Level Posted Date 2 days ago (8/17/2026 10:59 PM) ID 2026-74274 Job Location US-AZ-Scottsdale Required Clearance TS/SCI, obtainable within reasonable time based on requirements Category Engineering-Software Employment Type College Hiring Company General Dynamics Mission Systems, Inc. Basic Qualifications Basic Qualifications Requires a Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related Science, Engineering, Technology or Mathematics field. Also requires 1+ years of job-related experience, or a Master's degree. CLEARANCE REQUIREMENTS: Department of Defense TS/SCI security clearance is preferred at time of hire. Candidates must be able to obtain a TS/SCI clearance within a reasonable amount of time from date of hire. Applicants selected will be subject to a U.S. Government security investigation and must meet eligibility requirements for access to classified information. Due to the nature of work performed within our facilities, U.S. citizenship is required. Workplace Facility 100%, Flex Responsibilities for this Position ROLE AND POSITION OBJECTIVES: As a Systems and Test Integration Engineer on our TIDES team, you will be at the center of building the software and infrastructure that our nation's most advanced spacecraft programs depend on. You'll work with a talented team of hardware and systems engineers to design and deploy the DevOps Test Infrastructure (DOTI), a critical platform that accelerates hardware testing and ensures mission reliability. This role contributes directly to the Hardware Development Environment (HDE), which is a shared engineering backbone for all spacecraft payload programs at GDMS. This is a position for an early-career engineer eager to grow. You'll have the opportunity to learn from senior engineers, expanding your skills in test automation, CI/CD pipeline development, containerized deployments, and hardware-in-the-loop integration. Your contributions will have a real impact, supporting critical missions in a dynamic, team-oriented environment. Preferred Skills Experience: A bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical field, plus one year of relevant experience, or a master's degree. Experience developing software in Python, C/C++, or a similar language. A strong grasp of software fundamentals, including data structures, version control, testing, and debugging. Experience writing automated tests with frameworks like PyTest to ensure software quality. Familiarity with Git-based version control workflows, such as branching and merge requests. Exposure to CI/CD platforms like GitLab CI for automating builds, tests, and releases. Comfort working at the command line in Linux environments (RHEL, Ubuntu). An understanding of computer networking concepts (Ethernet, subnets, routing) and hardware interfaces. Exposure to containerization and orchestration tools like Docker, Kubernetes, or Helm is a significant plus. Experience working in an agile or scrum environment. Key Responsibilities Design and develop test software and automation frameworks for our shared test infrastructure. Build and maintain CI/CD pipelines in GitLab, including the management of self-hosted runners. Deploy and manage containerized services on our hardware test benches. Support the integration of our test software with real payload hardware and lab instrumentation. Develop test plans and procedures to verify system and subsystem requirements. Collaborate across teams, including with FPGA and hardware engineers, on system integration and platform features. Investigate and debug complex software and integration issues with a systematic approach. Create clear documentation for your designs and tooling to empower other engineers. What Sets You Apart You're curious about how the parts fit together. When you're writing test software, you want to know what hardware it drives, what the system needs it to do, and how your piece fits into the bigger picture. 632238a5-1d61-4694-a8d0-c8d596b89c37.description: Software Engineer (Early Career, Exceptional Talent) Boom Supersonic Software Engineer (Early Career, Exceptional Talent) Software Engineer (Early Career, Exceptional Talent) Your job is to build software that makes hardware, and to make us faster at building it. You will not work from a software department across the building. You will embed inside the team you build for: test crews streaming telemetry off a gas turbine at full power, design engineers turning a new turbine blade around overnight, technicians on a factory floor where the machines close out their own work orders. Their pain is your requirements document, and you will feel it firsthand, shipping code in your first week. We don't expect you to know hardware yet. We expect you to be excited to learn it, fast, starting the day you walk in. Most of your graduating class will go optimize ad clicks, dashboards, and checkout funnels. There is nothing wrong with that work except that it is the same work, at a thousand companies, behind the same login screens. We hire a small number of extraordinary computer science graduates who want the other thing: hard software problems attached to physical machines, with fire coming out one end. Boom exists to bring back commercial supersonic flight. Overture, our supersonic airliner, is the long game, and getting there means building turbomachinery faster than anyone ever has. Today that is Superpower, a natural gas turbine for next-generation AI data centers, on a development schedule nobody in the industry believes until they see it. The software problems on that path don't have playbooks. You will write them. This job is demanding and rewarding. This job isn't for everyone. You're the right person if: You want to build software that makes hardware, and learning the hardware side excites you more than it scares you You've done something extraordinary early: shipped software with real users, built the systems your club or lab depends on, or done work that most engineers don't see for years You'd rather ship something imperfect this week than something polished next month You want ownership, not guidance, and harder problems make you more energized, not less You find out what to build by watching your users struggle; waiting for a spec to arrive sounds miserable The test stand and the factory floor sound more interesting to you than a sprint planning meeting What You'll Do Own a defined piece of your team's software, with real accountability for the outcome Sit with the engineers, technicians, and test crews who use your software, and build what they actually need Ship code your first week, and a tool in daily use by the end of your first month Work with AI as a first-class part of the job: agents as coding partners, and interfaces designed for agents as well as humans Iterate fast: figure out what's wrong, fix it, and move on to the next problem You will thrive here if: You want ownership, not guidance You get more energized when a problem gets harder, not less You're comfortable not knowing the answer yet, and uncomfortable waiting for someone else to find it You'd rather watch a machinist fight a workflow for an hour than read a requirements document about it The ramp here is steep and the expectations are high from day one. Engineers who want a structured development program, a mentor rotation, and a clearly defined lane should look elsewhere. Engineers who want to spend their first year building software that makes hardware should apply. Work Location Internships require 100% onsite at Boom's headquarters located at 6803 S Tucson Way, Centennial, CO 80112. Compensation The Base Salary Range for this position is $92,000 - $124,000 per year. Actual salaries will vary based on factors including but not limited to location, experience, and performance. The range listed is just one component of Boom’s total rewards package for employees. Other rewards may include long-term incentives/equity, a flexible PTO policy, and many other progressive benefits. Additional perks include on-site meals and gym access. ITAR Requirement To conform to U.S. Government aerospace technology export regulations (ITAR and EAR), applicant must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the U.S., protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Due to the nature of this position, candidates must be eligible to access export-controlled information and technology as required by applicable U.S. export control laws . Learn more about ITAR here. Field Service Engineers London/South East Full-time Compensation: GBP 35,000 - GBP 41,000 - yearly Company Description TOMRA is a global leader in recycling and circular economy solutions. Founded in 1972, we design and deliver technology that helps keep valuable materials in circulation and reduces waste worldwide. With over 5,500 employees globally and operations in 60+ markets, TOMRA is now entering a major growth phase in the UK ahead of the planned Deposit Return Scheme launch in 2027. This is a unique opportunity to join the UK organisation as it scales and help build the teams that will support the next generation of recycling infrastructure. Job Description As a Field Engineer, you’ll play a vital role in supporting TOMRA’s mission to transform the way the world recycles—while always putting safety first. Whether working with equipment, customers, or travelling between sites, you’ll operate in a safety-focused environment where the wellbeing of our people and customers is a top priority. You’ll help keep our technology running smoothly by maintaining, repairing, and optimising equipment at customer sites. This is a hands-on, early-career role with a mix of planned and reactive work, offering variety, autonomy, and strong opportunities to learn and grow in a supportive team environment. You’ll be a key part of delivering a great customer experience while building your technical expertise. As the UK prepares for the introduction of the Deposit Return Scheme (DRS), TOMRA is entering an exciting growth phase and we're now looking for Field Service Engineers across London and the South East. What You’ll Be Doing As a Field Engineer, no two days are the same. You'll spend your time supporting customers, troubleshooting equipment, carrying out maintenance, and helping install new recycling technology. Working closely with experienced colleagues, you'll build your technical expertise while playing a key role in delivering an excellent customer experience and ensuring our equipment operates safely and reliably. Install, maintain, and repair TOMRA Reverse Vending Machines (RVMs) at customer sites. Support the installation, commissioning, and roll-out of new machines as TOMRA expands across the UK. Diagnose and resolve mechanical and electrical issues, carrying out both preventative maintenance and reactive repairs. Build strong relationships with customers and site contacts, providing professional and friendly service. Travel throughout your region to support customers, with occasional overnight stays when required. Accurately record service activities, machine status, and updates using digital systems and tools. Contribute to continuous improvement by sharing feedback, developing your technical knowledge, and maintaining high safety standards at all times. Ways of Working You'll follow established safety procedures, including TOMRA Safe and LOTO standards. You'll be supported with training, tools, and a collaborative team culture. Flexibility is essential in this role, as occasional approved overtime and weekend working will be required to support business needs. From October 2027, the position will transition to a rota-based shift pattern, which will include weekend coverage. Why This Role Is Exciting With the UK Deposit Return Scheme launching in October 2027, this is a unique opportunity to join TOMRA during a period of rapid growth and innovation. You'll gain hands-on experience with industry-leading technology, help shape the future of recycling in the UK, and build a rewarding technical career with a company making a positive environmental impact. Qualifications A curious and solution-oriented mindset, with strong attention to detail A customer-focused approach, with clear and confident communication skills A foundation in electro-mechanical systems, with an interest in learning how to analyse, test, and repair complex equipment Comfortable working both independently and as part of a wider, supportive team Flexibility to travel and manage your own schedule in a field-based role Full UK driving licence Additional Information Why TOMRA? Join a global leader committed to innovation and sustainability. At TOMRA, you’ll have the opportunity to make a real impact and contribute to a better future. What do you get from joining TOMRA? A growing UK organisation at an exciting scale‑up stage Purpose‑driven work with real environmental impact Supportive, inclusive and collaborative culture Opportunities to learn, develop and broaden your experience A role where your contribution is visible, valued and you have potential to grow Competitive salary and comprehensive benefits package, including: Health insurance (with the option to add family) Employer pension 10% non-contributory pension contributions Tenure Leave (can accrue more leave after from 5+ years of service) Company Bonus Paid overtime Ready to grow your career with purpose? Ability to write clear, meaningful commit messages and follow established branching and source-control practices. Willingness to learn the team's development workflow, including CI/CD and release processes. Our mission is clear -- we deliver IT to help P G win with the over 5 billion consumers we serve worldwide. Our IT professionals are diverse business leaders who apply IT expertise to deliver innovative, tech-focused business models and capabilities for our 65 iconic, trusted brands. From Day 1, you’ll be trusted to dive right in, take the lead, use your initiative, and build billion-dollar brands that help make everyday activities easier and make the world a better place! Our company offers purposeful work that will take your career places you never envisioned, in creative workspaces where innovation thrives and where your technical expertise is recognized and rewarded. The Opportunity As a Data Engineer, you'll design, develop, and implement cloud-based data and analytics platforms (DAP) and pipelines that acquire, cleanse, transform, and publish data from a wide variety of sources. Beyond building robust data solutions, you'll partner closely with business stakeholders, architects, and analytics teams to translate business needs into technical solutions, influence how data is structured and consumed, and help shape engineering standards across the team. Our stack keeps evolving, so we care less about which exact tools you know today and more about your curiosity and drive to keep learning and expanding your skill set. Key Responsibilities Partner with business stakeholders to understand their needs and translate them into robust, well-designed data solutions. Design, build, and maintain ETL/ELT pipelines on a modern cloud data platform. Integrate the data platform with other systems and services - ingesting from a range of sources (APIs, databases, files, third-party services) and making curated data available to downstream applications and consumers. Take end-to-end ownership of your work - from understanding the requirement, through design and implementation, to monitoring, supporting, and improving what you ship. Act as a technical point of contact for stakeholders, and help guide and mentor less-experienced engineers through knowledge sharing and code review. Help define and evolve our engineering standards and best practices for data - code quality, testing, CI/CD, and reusability. Ensure data quality, reliability, and performance across the solutions you own. Use modern development tools - IDEs (VS Code) and Git-based workflows - to build, test, and ship data solutions efficiently. Leverage Generative AI and agentic tooling to accelerate development, while applying good judgment on where and how to use it safely. Continuously learn and adopt new technologies, and share what you learn to help the whole team grow. Job Qualifications Required: Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or a related field. Experience in data engineering or a closely related field. Strong proficiency in Python and SQL for data processing, transformation, and analysis. Solid understanding of data engineering concepts - data modeling, ETL/ELT design, and distributed data processing. Good understanding of modern cloud platforms (Azure and/or GCP). Experience connecting data solutions with other systems - both ingesting from and delivering data to APIs, databases, and external services. Comfortable working with modern development tools - IDEs (e.g. VS Code), Git-based collaborative workflows, and CI/CD for data pipelines. Ownership mindset - ability to take a problem end-to-end, from understanding the business need to delivering and supporting a reliable solution. Excellent communication skills, with the ability to work closely with business stakeholders. Practical experience working with Generative AI tools, with a focus on AI-assisted development and agentic systems - and the judgment to use them effectively and safely. A genuine curiosity and willingness to learn - eager to pick up new technologies and continuously expand your technical stack. Ability to work in Cincinnati, OH based office on a hybrid schedule. Preferred: Hands-on experience with Azure Databricks. Proficiency with PySpark / Spark for large-scale data processing. Experience with Power BI. Background in software development / software engineering (application development, APIs, testing, design patterns) beyond pure data pipelines. Relevant certifications, e.g. Databricks Certified Data Engineer (Associate/Professional) or Microsoft Azure / Google Cloud Data Engineer. The Agent Infra team builds the infrastructure that runs autonomous AI agents at Roblox for millions of creators building experiences on our platform, and for thousands of Roblox engineers shipping production code every day. Agent workloads break the assumptions most infrastructure is built on. They run for hours instead of milliseconds, they're non-deterministic, they execute code nobody wrote, and they need real credentials against real systems to be useful at all. Making that safe, durable, and cost effective at Roblox’s scale is the hard problem our team is solving. Someone who builds things: You have projects, internships, or open-source work you'd genuinely enjoy walking us through. Into AI agents. You've built something with them, even something small, and you can tell us what broke. Comfortable writing real code in Go, Python, Rust, or similar, and quick to pick up whatever you haven't used yet. A fast learner who asks good questions, digs into things you don't understand, and doesn't wait to be told what to do next. You Will Build and shape the platform that runs Roblox’s agents; across internal and external products at massive scale. Work on agentic infrastructure, ensuring that we’re able to build optimal, security and scalable systems, whilst keeping pace with new advances in the industry. Continually learn and adjust your understanding of the systems we are building and what is capable with AI agents. Our products range from complex structured credit facilities for growth-focused businesses to mortgages for professional landlords and property investors, as well as simple loans for consumers delivered digitally. We fuel our lending through customer deposits, which we attract by delivering a premium experience, choice and consistently great value to smart savers. The business model we have created is unique and difficult to replicate, with our ‘best of both’ approach combining deep human expertise with advanced digital, tech and data capabilities. This combination not only allows us to deliver excellent customer experiences, but to do so efficiently and at scale. We are proud of our innovative and agile culture, which drives consistently high employee engagement scores and makes Shawbrook an attractive destination for the best talent. If you’re willing to roll up your sleeves, contribute new ideas and believe anything is possible, you’re our kind of person. Work with us because you: Want to be part of a bank built for the dynamics of the modern world Relish a challenge and enjoy a fast-paced, innovative and hardworking culture Enjoy finding new and better ways to solve complexity and make things happen Want to belong to a diverse culture that stands shoulder to shoulder with minority and underrepresented groups Care about society and the environment and want to be part of a business that cares too Want to continue to grow professionally and be the best version of yourself Job Description We are looking for a talented AI Engineer to join our AI Engineering squad as we scale our in-house artificial intelligence capability across Shawbrook Bank. Working in close partnership with our AI Product Manager, and alongside other AI Engineers and the AI Engineering Lead, you will help design, build, and ship AI solutions within a regulated banking environment. This is a hands-on role for a strong engineer who is excited about building with AI. You'll work across our AI products and shared platform capabilities, getting hands-on with LLMs, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and modern AI tooling. You’ll be starting with well-scoped work and growing towards owning features end-to-end, with support from experienced engineers around you. Key Responsibilities Build, test, and ship features across our AI products and shared platform capabilities, progressing from well-scoped tasks towards larger slices of work. Work hands-on with LLMs, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and AI tooling, with support from senior engineers. Build a good working understanding of our AI platform and applications, with growing awareness of other domains across the Bank (lending, data, risk, and operations) Contribute to the controls production AI depends on (evaluation, observability, testing, and CI/CD). Help integrate AI services with other systems and data sources through well-designed APIs. Take an active part in code review and pairing, growing towards end-to-end ownership. Apply responsible-AI practices within a regulated environment. Support engineers in the wider Shawbrook Engineering department with AI adoption and upskilling. Work within an agile, cross-functional squad to deliver iteratively and aligned to business value. Qualifications Essential Confident building and maintaining backend services and APIs, ideally in Python or .NET, with good testing and version-control practices. You have worked with AI programmatically, for example building with LLM APIs, machine learning, or AI-driven projects (professional, academic, or personal). Some experience with a major cloud platform, preferably Azure. Keen to take on more responsibility over time and grow into owning work end-to-end. A friendly teammate who enjoys learning and working with others. Relevant academic background in Computer Science, Data Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or related discipline. Nice to have Experience delivering AI/ML in a production environment. Professional certifications in cloud platforms (e.g., Azure AI Engineer Associate) would be beneficial. Background in machine learning engineering/operations. Interest in developing a broad skillset across AI, backend, and frontend engineering. Experience in regulated environments. Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever. Join Micron’s Memory Systems Engineering team and contribute to the development of premier digital and mixed-signal foundations for our high-bandwidth memory (HBM) products. This position offers an outstanding chance to work intimately with multiple engineering areas, guaranteeing the smooth integration and implementation of HBM base die. Collaborate with design verification teams on verification planning, coverage goals, CDC/RDC checks, and debugging of RTL, testbench, and gate-level issues. Support silicon bring-up and post-silicon validation through debug enablement, root cause analysis, and collaboration with DFT and test teams. Knowledge of SystemVerilog RTL development, clock/reset architecture, CDC/RDC methodologies, and low-power design concepts. Understanding of design-for-debug and design-for-test principles and ability to collaborate with multi-functional engineering teams. Experience working in environments that are AI Assisted or AI Enabled, or willingness to harness AI tools to support engineering productivity, debug workflows, and data-driven analysis. Interest in refining micro-architecture to improve timing and understanding design tradeoffs related to constraints and path intent. 0933be4c-1f04-4b8f-a07d-b6b97beede8d.description: Data Science Engineer II (Full Time) - United States Skip to main content Careers English Sign In Search for Jobs Data Science Engineer II (Full Time) - United States page is loaded Data Science Engineer II (Full Time) - United States Apply remote type Hybrid locations San Jose, California, US time type Full time posted on Posted Yesterday time left to apply End Date: August 22, 2026 (2 days left to apply) job requisition id 2023062 The application window is expected to close on: 08/22/2026 Job posting may be removed earlier if the position is filled or if a sufficient number of applications are received . Meet the Team We are looking for an early in career Data Science Analyst to help turn product, customer, operational, and business data into clear insights that support better decision-making across Enterprise Security. This is an opportunity to work with multi-functional teams, learn about cybersecurity and SaaS product analytics, and contribute to data-driven decisions that improve product quality, customer outcomes, operational efficiency, and business visibility. Your Impact As a Data Science Analyst, you will partner with Product, Engineering, Quality, Finance, and Operations teams to collect, analyze, and interpret data from multiple sources. You will help build dashboards, prepare recurring reports, identify trends, and translate findings into clear insights for technical and non-technical collaborators. In this role, you will gain exposure to cybersecurity, enterprise SaaS, product analytics, financial and operational metrics, and cross-functional decision-making. Your work will help teams better understand product usage, customer adoption, operational performance, cost trends, and opportunities to improve how we deliver value to customers. You will have the opportunity to grow your analytical, technical, and business skills while contributing to high-impact initiatives across the Enterprise Security organization. Key Responsibilities Collect, clean, validate, and analyze data from multiple sources, including product telemetry, usage data, customer data, operational metrics, and business reports. Build and maintain dashboards, reports, and recurring analyses to track key product, quality, adoption, financial, and operational metrics. Support analysis of COGS and gross margin across customer cohorts and the overall business, helping identify trends, drivers, risks, and opportunities for improvement. Partner with Product, Engineering, Quality, Finance, and Operations teams to understand business questions and translate them into data-driven analysis. Help define and track metrics that measure product usage, customer adoption, quality, operational efficiency, and business outcomes. Analyze trends and summarize findings to support planning, forecasting, roadmap discussions, and business-impact measurement. Translate data findings into clear insights, summaries, and recommendations for both technical and non-technical audiences. Automate recurring reporting and data-analysis workflows using SQL, Python, R, or similar tools. Identify data-quality issues and work with partners to improve data accuracy, consistency, and usability. Maintain documentation of data sources, assumptions, calculations, dashboards, and analysis methods. Use AI-assisted tools responsibly to improve data analysis, summarization, automation, and reporting workflows. Minimum Qualifications Meet one of the following (completed within the past 3 years or expected to be completed within the next 12 months ): A Master's degree with 0 years of work experience ; or A Bachelor's degree with 2 years of work experience. Qualifying education and work experience should be in Data Science, Computer Science, Engineering, Statistics, Mathematics, Business Analytics, Economics, or a related field. Experience using SQL for querying and validation, alongside competency in an analytical scripting language like Python or R. Experience designing dashboards and reports using industry-standard platforms such as Tableau, Power BI, or Splunk. Strong critical thinking and problem-solving skills required to navigate sophisticated data Preferred Qualifications Previous internship, research, or work experience in data/business analytics, with exposure to product, SaaS, or operational data environments. Familiarity with statistical modeling, forecasting, and machine learning, combined with the ability to lead large, sophisticated datasets and ensure data integrity. Proven success partnering with cross-functional teams and translating sophisticated technical analyses into clear, stakeholder-ready recommendations. Strong curiosity about the cybersecurity landscape, including enterprise security, AI, and modern data platforms. Why Cisco? At Cisco, we’re revolutionizing how data and infrastructure connect and protect organizations in the AI era – and beyond. We’ve been innovating fearlessly for 40 years to create solutions that power how humans and technology work together across the physical and digital worlds. These solutions provide customers with unparalleled security, visibility, and insights across the entire digital footprint. Fueled by the depth and breadth of our technology, we experiment and create meaningful solutions. Add to that our worldwide network of doers and experts, and you’ll see that the opportunities to grow and build are limitless. We work as a team, collaborating with empathy to make really big things happen on a global scale. Because our solutions are everywhere, our impact is everywhere. We are Cisco, and our power starts with you.
